title: Five Ways To Use AI Coding Agents to Improve Your Software Architecture
gist: Pureur, Bittner and Miller argue AI coding agents only produce sound architecture when fed explicit, measurable Quality Attribute Requirements and trade-offs, and lay out five uses: documenting legacy services, finding architectural flaws, security audits, architectural scaffolding, and testable Minimum Viable Architectures. Their core claim is that coding gets simpler while requirements work becomes dramatically harder.

insights.claim: AI coding agents fed only functional requirements will not produce sound architecture; teams must supply measurable Quality Attribute Requirements (QARs) and trade-offs and then test the generated code against them.
insights.speaker: Pierre Pureur
insights.so_what: Value capture in AI coding shifts toward tooling that encodes and verifies non-functional requirements, not raw code generation.
